comparison: Perfect agreement on decoder validation (C32-C35). Both evaluations find the decoding approach convincing and well-suited to address research questions, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the state-of-the-art methods and extensive localizer design.

Perfect agreement on behavioral learning results (C28-C31). Both evaluations support the learning performance findings. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment while peer reviewers implicitly accept these results without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on consolidation effects (C45). Both evaluations rate this as UNCERTAIN due to nonsignificant results and inconclusive analyses, acknowledging design limitations that prevent strong conclusions.

Strong agreement on sequential replay findings (C36-C39, C9-C10). Both evaluations support the performance-dependent sequential replay and its replication of Wimmer et al. 2020. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm replay was present in low performers, aligning with OpenEval's assessment of the negative correlation with performance.

Strong agreement on clustered reactivation (C40-C43, C6-C8). Both evaluations support the distance-modulated clustered reactivation findings. OpenEval notes the weak interaction (p=0.13) as a limitation, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'limited amounts of data' but still find the evidence 'convincing' with clear demonstration of simultaneous reactivation timing.

Strong agreement on primary conclusions about clustered reactivation (C49-C50, C56-C57, C75-C76). Both evaluations support the main findings. OpenEval finds the breadth-first interpretation reasonable, while peer reviewers describe it as 'novel evidence' and note the revised manuscript convincingly demonstrates simultaneous reactivation.

Agreement on sequential replay and performance relationship (C58-C59, C77). Both evaluations support the replication of performance-related sequential replay. OpenEval notes the memory trace stability inference (C59) is somewhat speculative, which aligns with peer concerns about interpretive claims.

Strong agreement on study limitations (C68-C73). Both evaluations support the authors' transparent acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewers extensively discuss the same concerns OpenEval identifies: limited trial numbers, underpowered analyses, and design constraints affecting retrieval phase analysis.

Partial agreement on speculative interpretations (C66-C67, C78-C79 vs C59, C66-C67). Both rate speculative claims as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval identifies these as hypotheses requiring future testing. Peer reviewers raise conceptual concerns about mutual exclusivity assumptions and request substantiation of strong claims about reactivation types.

Divergent evaluations on analytical approach (C74). OpenEval rates the lack of preregistration limitation as SUPPORTED (appropriately disclosed). Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising methodological concerns about whether the analytical approach can definitively distinguish sequential from clustered reactivation, questioning potential bias from time window selection.
OpenEval evaluates questionnaire data on alertness and affect (C46-C48) as SUPPORTED with straightforward descriptive statistics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates extensive methodological details (C80-C117) as SUPPORTED, noting methods follow established practices with appropriate statistical approaches and quality control. No corresponding detailed peer review evaluation of these specific methodological claims found, though peer reviewers generally praise the methodological approach.

OpenEval evaluates literature review and theoretical framework claims (C1-C3, C11-C26, C51-C55, C60-C65) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate characterization of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims found.

OpenEval evaluates experimental design description (C4-C5, C27) as SUPPORTED, noting the graph structure represents a novel extension of prior paradigms. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these design description claims found.
